checks.result: 1.42 km and 11/11 staged encounters in 332.0 simulated seconds. CARLA recorded 0 ego contacts, 0 red-light violations and 0 missed yields.
A moving vehicle and a moving pedestrian were both within 50 m for 49.9% of the drive, versus 3.4% previously. One exposure had 2 moving vehicles and 6 moving pedestrians nearby.

At 50–100 m, correctly placed 3D road-user drawings increased from 59 to 181 on the same drive, across 9,070 front-sector actor-frames including occlusions. Across all ranges, unmatched drawings increased from 435 to 454.
In a matched test, median speed alongside the six drums rose from 5.1 to 14.7 km/h. Minimum body clearance was 0.27 m. The driver held a stop for 9.9 seconds at the blocked lane.

On the original route, median speed on a different boulevard segment fell from 37.7 to 31.6 km/h. At 434 m the front detector reported a person. The three-camera test retained its input features and controls but has no image to verify that classification.
On the original film, 420 fresh camera-and-lidar readings matched the six drums. 0 were unmatched. Fresh readings covered 420/1185 nearby drum-frames.
The populated drive produced 237 fresh RGB-and-lidar matches to the six real props. 0 readings missed the position gate. Within 20 m, 236 of 621 drum-frames had fresh measurements.

On the same Urban Pace sensor tape, the lead car first appeared as a correctly placed 3D body at 49.8 m, versus 43.1 m with the older display. The front camera can also show a bearing before the sensors have enough range evidence for a 3D body.

scope: The site replays closed-loop simulated drives. Population counts include occluded traffic. A 3D symbol needs measured range. First-sighting distances depend on the individual road user, view and occlusion.
